title: Tame fixed subschemes form a weakly boundary normal crossings family
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular separated scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $B$ be a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$, preserving $B$, tamely and generically freely. Tame means that each geometric stabilizer has order invertible in the residue field; generically free means free on a dense invariant open. Suppose $B$ is $G$-strict: distinct translates of a component are disjoint. For each nontrivial subgroup $H\leq G$ let $X^H$ be the closed subscheme equalizing all $h:X\to X$ with the identity, with empty fixed subschemes omitted. Then $X^H$ is regular and nowhere dense and has normal crossings with $B$. Scheme-theoretically $X^H\cap X^K=X^{\langle H,K\rangle}$, so the same assertions hold for every nonempty intersection. At a geometric point fixed by $H$, its tangent space is the $H$-invariant subspace of the tangent space of $X$. The union of the supports of these fixed subschemes is precisely the complement of the largest free open. They are permuted by $G$ via $gX^H=X^{gHg^{-1}}$. Here a regular closed subscheme has normal crossings with $B$ when, at every point on it, its ideal and the ideals of the boundary components through the point are generated by subsets of one regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Tangent space at a geometric point over $x$ means the dual of $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$ after extending scalars to the geometric residue field.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2, printed pp.76--77; VIII Lemma 4.2.3 and proof, printed p.119 (with VI 4.1 for fixed subschemes).

proof.text: For any test scheme $S$, a map $S\to X$ factors through $X^H$ precisely when $h\circ f=f$ for every $h\in H$. These equalizers are closed: each is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of the separated scheme $X$ under $(h,\mathrm{id})$, and their finite intersection is closed. Being fixed by both $H$ and $K$ is equivalent to being fixed by every word in $H\cup K$ and their inverses. Thus the same equalizer functor defines $X^H\cap X^K=X^{\langle H,K\rangle}$, including its scheme structure. Also $h(gf)=gf$ is equivalent to $(g^{-1}hg)f=f$, proving $gX^H=X^{gHg^{-1}}$.

source.place: VI 4.1, printed p.76; VIII 4.2.3, first paragraph, p.119.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X^H$, and choose a geometric point over it. Every $h\in H$ fixes $x$ and its residue field: equality on the geometric point implies equality on its embedded residue field. On $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ the ideal of $X^H$ is consequently $I=I_H=(h(a)-a)$, with $a\in R$; the equalizer equations localize to these equations (differences of fractions follow by the quotient rule). The order of $H$ divides the geometric stabilizer order, so is invertible in $k=\kappa(x)$. Apply [lem-per-tame-fixed-local-regularity]: $R/I$ is regular and its cotangent is $T/D$, where $T=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and $D=\operatorname{span}(h-1)T$. Dualizing identifies its tangent with the functionals on $T$ annihilating all $(h-1)v$, exactly $(T^*)^H$. This remains the stated identification after extending the residue field, since finite linear equations commute with field extension. Thus $X^H$ is regular everywhere and has the claimed tangent spaces.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2, pp.76--77; VIII 4.2.3, p.119, tangent-space paragraph.

proof.text: At this $x$, [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion] supplies boundary equations $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ among regular parameters, so their classes in $T$ are independent. Apply [lem-trf-etale-component-coordinate-identification] with the identity etale neighborhood: after shrinking, the components through $x$ are exactly the individual coordinate hyperplanes. By $G$-strictness each component through $x$ is $H$-stable: its translate still passes through $x$ and hence cannot be a distinct translate. Thus $h(t_i)=u_{h,i}t_i$ for a unit $u_{h,i}$, and $k\bar t_i$ is a character line with character $\chi_i(h)=\overline{u}_{h,i}$. Define $e=|H|^{-1}\sum_hh$ on $T$. Directly $e^2=e$, $e(h-1)=0$ and $v-ev=|H|^{-1}\sum_h(v-hv)$, so $T=T^H\oplus D$ and $D=\ker e$. A trivial character line lies in $T^H$; every other line lies in $D$ (the sum of a nontrivial character is zero, because multiplication by a character value different from 1 permutes the sum). Relabel so $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_l$ are trivial. For $i>l$, choose $h$ with $\chi_i(h)\ne1$. Then $u_{h,i}-1$ is a unit and $(u_{h,i}-1)t_i=h(t_i)-t_i\in I$, proving $t_i\in I$.

source.place: VIII 4.2.3, p.119, boundary-character and invariant-complement paragraphs; last vanishing argument written using a unit.

proof.text: Extend $\bar t_{l+1},\ldots,\bar t_n$ to a basis of $D$ and $\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_l$ to a basis of $T^H$. Lift the extra $D$-basis vectors to $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in I$: step 2 identifies the image of $I$ in $T$ with $D$. Lift the extra invariant basis vectors arbitrarily to $s_{r+1},\ldots,s_m\in\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] this full list has $\dim R$ members; by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] it generates $\mathfrak m$ and hence is a regular system of parameters. Since $R/I$ is regular, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] supplies some parameter generators $p_1,\ldots,p_c$ for $I$. Their classes are independent in $T$, so $I/\mathfrak m I\to T$ is injective: express any representative as $\sum a_jp_j$; if its class in $T$ is zero, independence forces all $a_j\in\mathfrak m$. Its image is $D$. Therefore the chosen $t_{l+1},\ldots,t_n,s_1,\ldots,s_r$ give a basis of $I/\mathfrak mI$, and Nakayama, applied to the finite ideal $I$ in the Noetherian ring $R$, gives $I=(t_{l+1},\ldots,t_n,s_1,\ldots,s_r)$. This is the required simultaneous coordinate description with the boundary equations. It proves normal crossings at every point.

source.place: VIII 4.2.3, p.119, basis-extension and ideal-generation paragraphs; Stacks Tags 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), 00DV (lemma-NAK), via existing nodes.

proof.text: Let $U$ be a dense invariant open on which the action is free. For $H\ne1$, $X^H$ is disjoint from $U$, since a geometric point of $X^H$ has stabilizer containing $H$. Its closed support is thus nowhere dense. There are finitely many subgroups. Let $F$ be the finite union of these supports. Its complement is invariant and open by step 1. A geometric point lies outside $F$ exactly when its stabilizer is trivial: a nontrivial stabilizer fixes that geometric point, and membership in a fixed subscheme is exactly that condition. Thus $X\setminus F$ is free, and any free open is contained in it, proving maximality and the asserted union formula. Finally every nonempty intersection of the family equals the fixed subscheme of the subgroup generated by its indices, by step 1. For a nonempty list of nontrivial subgroups this subgroup is nontrivial. Steps 2--4 and this step apply to it and give all weakly boundary normal crossings assertions; the empty intersection is $X$ itself.

proof_origin.place: VI 4.1--4.2 and VIII Lemma 4.2.3, pp.76--77,118--119; the final boundary-vanishing argument is the elementary unit form, with ideal generation made explicit by Stacks 00NR and 00DV.
